Every writer class carries its fence mechanism per docs/composition/PR2_RESOLVER_AND_EPOCH_DESIGN.md §3. A new writer of the identity surface that is absent from this census fails CI.

derivedClassified.classification: DERIVED, transitively fenced — projectActiveRules is a pure function of rules docs + non-archived bundles (status/ruleIds/ruleHardness/name) + agent.equippedTraits — ALL epoch-fenced stores — and the written value additionally passes through resolveForDeploy, which is pure and REMOVAL-ONLY (it can never add content); a window write can only re-derive values the frozen inputs imply. The residual scan reads authority stores through the resolver, never activeRules (census host A: derived). FENCED FILE — a literal in-file check is the optional PR-4 sanctioned-entry splice, not a PR-2 edit.
derivedClassified.founderRuling: REVERSED — Sol design-review adjudication, Aug 6, 2026 (supersedes the same-day acceptance): DERIVED classification stands for DARK OPERATION ONLY. The PR-4 fenced splice is REQUIRED — epoch/generation validation before the activeRules write + a generation stamp on the written projection; readers reject stale-generation projections. Recorded reason: Sol's cross-generation counterexample — a decide.js window in flight across the activation boundary re-derives from pre-activation reads and commits the stale projection after the new generation activates, unmarked. See docs/composition/ACTIVATION_PRECONDITIONS.md (ruling of record).
